   CONSENT ITEMS  AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE A SPONSOR
  DISCUSSED  AGREEMENT WITH THE CALIFORNIA CONSERVATION CORPS
  SEPARATELY  FOR NON-NATIVE VEGETATION REMOVAL IN THE ARROYO
r~

  SECO AND ACCEPT AN $84,500 DONATION FROM THE ONE
  ARROYO FOUNDATION FOR GOAT GRAZING (PRCS Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed vegetation management and goat
  grazing activities are exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Article 19,
  Class 1 (Existing Facilities) (§15301) and Class 4 (Minor Alterations
  to Land) (§15304), and are further statutorily exempt as specific
  actions necessary to prevent or mitigate a wildfire emergency under
  Public Resources Code §21080(b)(4) and CEQA Guidelines
  §15269(c);
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to execute a sponsor agreement
  between the City of Pasadena and the California Conservation
  Corps (CCC) to assist with non-native vegetation removal and
  habitat restoration activities in the Arroyo Seco (Contract No.
  24,327); and
  (3) Authorize the City Manager to accept the donation of $84,500
  from One Arroyo Foundation for goat grazing services in the Arroyo
  Seco.

  The following individuals spoke in support of the staff
r  recommendation and expressed the importance of vegetation
  removal and brush maintenance in the Arroyo:

  Carlos Javelera, Pasadena resident
  Daniel Rossman, One Arroyo Foundation

  Mike Polka, Pasadena resident, expressed his support for the
  removal of non-native vegetation and advocated for the
  removal of invasive trees in the Arroyo.

  In response to Councilmember Cole's inquiry regarding fire danger,
  Chad Augustin, Fire Chief, reported that the Fire Department will be
  looking outside of traditional fire and risk mitigation efforts. Koko
  Panossian, Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director,
  added that the proposed contract is an enhancement to the existing
  brush abatement program.

  In response to Mayor Gordo's inquiry regarding the availability of
  wildlife cameras allowing the public to watch the goat grazing, Jose
  Mireles, Parks Superintendent, reported Royal Foothill Conservancy
  has such cameras in the area, and that City staff has already
  reached out regarding the possibility of making the footage publicly
  accessible.
